title: 4th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 09:03 to 10:31 with 34 members present. The Speaker announced two committee membership changes, and a motion from the Keyodhoo member asking Parliament to debate the timing of when GST becomes payable was put to a vote and not accepted (11 for, 36 against), so no debate took place. Members then continued debating the Baarashu member's resolution seeking MPs' views on the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) after 15 years, with the Vaikaradhoo, Dhiggaru, Hulhumale', Manadhoo, Milandhoo, Inguraidhoo, Hulhudhoo, Thulhaadhoo and Holhudhoo members speaking on council costs, councillor numbers and atoll councils. The debate was not finished; the Speaker ended the sitting early to make room for committee work.

items.title: Attendance of members at the sitting
items.outcome: 34 present, 10 on leave, 4 on official travel

items.title: Announcement of changes to committee membership (Human Rights and Gender Committee; Judiciary Committee)
items.outcome: announced: Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdhooh replaces Central Maafannu member Asma Rasheed on Human Rights and Gender; Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir replaces Vaikaradhoo member Hussain Ziyad on Judiciary

items.title: Motion by Keyodhoo member Mohamed Niushad to debate when GST becomes payable, in light of difficulties businesses face
items.outcome: not accepted for debate, 11 for / 36 against

items.title: Resolution by Baarashu member Ibrahim Shujau seeking MPs' views on the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) 15 years after it took effect (continued debate)

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Cited the high annual cost of running the council system and said large block-grant sums sit unspent in council bank accounts.
Said atoll councils hold little real power and asked whether atoll offices could be used more productively.
Argued fewer councillors paid better would let councils attract capable staff and work more productively.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the resolution seeks MPs' views and is not about reducing councillors; favoured fewer councillors in islands under 2,000 people.
Cited national debt and revenue gaps as reasons for review and defended the government's approach to councils.
In his second turn, argued about previous governments' borrowing and said council buildings are being rebuilt.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Presented the motion on when GST becomes payable, citing business complaints about paying GST on invoices before being paid, especially by government bodies.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said councils take about 5% of the state budget and questioned singling them out while ministries also vary in performance.
Argued reducing councillors would also cut seats held by women, and that councils differ widely in income and context.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Opposed the resolution, saying he saw no benefit shown from cutting councillors and that islands have gained services under the current system.
Said the Local Government Ministry's budget is planned to rise sharply and suggested the resolution aims to create political posts before elections.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said the resolution is about reviewing how the system works, not cutting women's seats or councillor numbers.
Criticised some councils for party politicisation, refusing tasks and hiring near elections, and asked for legal limits close to elections.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the resolution as a way to consult the public, saying service quality matters more than councillor numbers.
Said the law suited conditions when it was passed and that today's economic situation justifies reviewing council numbers.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised a point of order during the Dhiggaru member's speech, about the number of councillors in Hithadhoo; the Speaker did not accept it.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order saying remarks about previous governments were not directed at him and he had no role in those projects.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the government has supported councils and the resolution is not about cutting costs or taking power from councils.
Said Hulhudhoo and Meedhoo want their own council separate from Addu City.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Raised long-delayed handover of completed housing units in Thulhaadhoo and lack of housing plots in Goidhoo, Fulhadhoo and Fehendhoo, and asked the government to act.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Said atoll councils give island councils little help and councils need more budget, power and limits on staff hiring.
Said Male' has more councillors than MPs and that the system should be reviewed.

decisions: Committee membership changes announced: Funadhoo member replaces Central Maafannu member on Human Rights and Gender; Kendhoo member replaces Vaikaradhoo member on Judiciary.
The Keyodhoo member's GST timing motion was not accepted for debate (11 for, 36 against, 0 abstaining).
Debate on the Baarashu member's Decentralisation Act resolution continued but was not concluded.
Sitting ended early to give time to committee work; next sitting set for 18 June 2025 at 09:00.

votes.what: Whether to debate the Keyodhoo member's motion on when GST becomes payable (24 needed; 47 voted; 93 members, 50 present)
